Art

Private art import and PaperZD integration

Import only audited privately licensed source assets; all exact source frame coordinates remain blocked in this edition.

On this page

PNG import and slicing

  1. Copy licensed sources into a private source-art workspace retaining pack/path provenance and hashes. Do not put paid originals in the public docs repository.
  2. Import a selected PNG into Content/Game/Art privately. Apply the Paper2D texture settings where the installed Editor exposes them; inspect filtering/compression, sRGB, mipmaps and alpha rather than assuming every sheet requires the same setting.
  3. Start pixel art with nearest filtering and compare mip behavior at all camera zooms; no-mip output may shimmer at reduced scale, so choose from measured scene readability. Keep UI portraits and world sprites separately tunable.
  4. Use the actual layout guide to extract sprites at known cell rectangles. Transparent gaps can confuse automatic extraction; prefer explicit grid/manual rectangles for a documented sheet. Name sprite action/facing/frame and record the source rectangle.
  5. Set a shared custom foot pivot and Pixels Per Unreal Unit based on actual measured body height and the collision capsule. Align feet to the capsule floor, not the sprite image center; do not resize physics to compensate for inconsistent art pivots.
  6. Create ordered flipbooks with verified frames/timing, then PaperZD sequences and the single action/facing resolver after checking the installed source/editor API. Clothing/weapon layers use matching frame rectangles/page and one shared clock.

Materials, depth and shadows

Prototype a masked, depth-tested sprite material in 3D first; compare unlit readable color to lightly lit material on the actual art. Translucent layers can sort incorrectly against other sprites and world geometry; do not solve all cases by assigning extreme global sort priorities. Keep layer offsets tiny and consistent in sprite-plane space to avoid z-fighting.

A vertical or deliberately camera-facing presentation plane is a cosmetic choice. Test it at the fixed elevation on slopes, stairs, under bridges and behind walls. Keep the collision capsule upright and independent. Prototype a simple ground-contact blob shadow or separate shadow proxy when sprite shadow artifacts are unacceptable; no universal shadow solution is claimed.

Occluder fade is local client material presentation. Server collision and LOS remain intact. Keep roof/interior occlusion readable and ensure a transparent wall does not imply attacks pass through it.

Plugin verification gate

Record PaperZD descriptor VersionName, supported engine/build, module names, animation source/sequence types, AnimInstance binding, directional resolver APIs and callback threading from the installed release. Public product documentation is not proof of compatibility with this installation. If unavailable, keep Paper2D debug presentation and explicitly block PaperZD acceptance.

GAS abilities publish action tags/times to the presentation bridge. Do not use a skeletal PlayMontage ability task for sprite playback without a verified custom bridge. A sprite notify may play a footstep or spark, but gameplay timing and action release remain authority-owned.

Reimport and acceptance

Reimport one body sheet and compare manifest hash/frame count/pivots before replacing sequences. Test body+hair+outfit+cloak+weapon in all four directions and every registered page. Check remote player appearance after reconnect and cross-zone transfer. Capture missing assets by ID and repair mappings, not by adding another competing animation system.
